analysis.investment_thesis: Optiemus trades at 55.6x earnings and 5.1x book — more than 3.6x its Graham Number of ~₹114 — offering zero margin of safety for a low-margin distributor with a deeply scarred earnings record. The business has not demonstrated the sustained earning power required to justify speculative ownership at any price near current levels.
key_strengths: Debt/Equity of 0.32 is the one ratio that passes my threshold (<0.5), and cash improved to ₹144 Cr in FY25
Revenue has recovered from a trough of ₹182 Cr (FY21) back toward the ₹1,890 Cr (FY25) range, showing the business is not terminal
Three consecutive years of reported profit (FY23–25: ₹42/57/63 Cr) — the first such streak in over a decade
key_risks: Chronic earnings instability: losses in FY19 (-₹59 Cr), FY20 (-₹85 Cr), FY22 (-₹1 Cr) — no 5-year consecutive profit record exists
Free cash flow deeply negative three of last four years (FY23: -₹99 Cr, FY25: -₹96 Cr) — reported profits are not converting to cash
Thin 5.28% operating margin in a commodity electronics distribution business with no evident competitive moat
red_flags: P/E of 55.6x versus my maximum of 15x; P/B of 5.1x versus my maximum of 1.5x — both fail by multiples, not margins
Graham Number ≈ ₹114 (sqrt(22.5 × EPS ₹7.1 × BVPS ₹80.7)); current price ₹414 is 3.6x this ceiling
FY21 'profit' of ₹95 Cr was entirely manufactured by ₹206 Cr of other income against a -₹98 Cr operating loss — earnings quality is poor
Finance costs surged from ₹8 Cr (FY21) to ₹30 Cr (FY25) as borrowings rose to ₹247 Cr — debt is re-accumulating
Nine-year revenue CAGR of -0.2%: the company sells roughly the same rupees today as it did in 2016, suggesting no durable growth engine
analysis.detailed_analysis:
By every quantitative standard I have applied for fifty years, Optiemus Infracom is a speculation masquerading as an investment. The Graham Number of approximately ₹114 — derived from FY25 EPS of ₹7.1 and book value per share of ~₹81 — sets the ceiling of fair value; the market is asking ₹414, a 264% premium. A P/E of 55.6x and P/B of 5.1x are not merely elevated — they price in years of flawless execution for a business whose nine-year revenue CAGR is literally negative. Mr. Market is in an exuberant mood here, and the intelligent investor must decline the invitation.

The earnings record disqualifies the stock on its own. My discipline demands five consecutive years of positive earnings before I will consider a purchase; Optiemus recorded operating losses from FY19 through FY21 and another near-zero year in FY22. The sole exception — FY21's ₹95 Cr net profit — was a mirage built on ₹206 Cr of non-operating other income against a -₹98 Cr operating result. True operating profitability is only three years old and already showing strain: net profit growth is decelerating, free cash flow was -₹96 Cr in FY25, and finance costs have quadrupled since FY21 as the company re-levers to fund capex (CWIP jumped to ₹99 Cr). This is precisely the type of situation where a novice sees a "recovery story" and a value investor sees a business still proving itself — at a price that assumes the proof is already complete.
